title: U.S. House · Florida's 21st District
area: The Treasure Coast and northern Palm Beach County, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.
Incumbent Rep. Brian Mast (R)'s Republican primary was canceled and he advanced unopposed. James Martin won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Bernard Taylor.
David Fabrikant is running as a write-in candidate with no party affiliation.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to expanding U.S. security assistance to Israel.
positions.quote: I am committed to expanding America’s security assistance to Israel.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to repealing and replacing the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: I am committed to repealing and replacing the Affordable Care Act to give every American access to quality, affordable healthcare.

record.text: Serves as Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and also sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee for the 2025–2026 Congress.
Says he opposed the Iran Nuclear Deal and voted for sanctions on Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

candidates.name: James Martin

priorities.text: Says he opposes tariffs and supports using antitrust enforcement to address corporate consolidation driving up costs for working families.
Says he will work to complete Everglades restoration, clean up Lake Okeechobee, and stop toxic discharges into the St. Lucie Estuary and Indian River Lagoon.
Says he supports getting money out of politics, banning members of Congress from trading stocks, and closing the revolving door between Congress and lobbying.

positions.summary: Says he wants to end tariffs he describes as reckless and as driving up grocery prices.
Says he supports a public option so every American who wants it has a pathway to affordable coverage.
positions.quote: he supports a public option: a pathway to quality, affordable healthcare for every American who wants it

statements.quote: creating a workable path to legal status for long-term residents who’ve built their lives here
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

candidates.researchNotes: Added a statement on immigration from his campaign site; he does not state a position on enforcement or deportation levels as such.

candidates.name: Alexander Cooke

priorities.text: Says he will focus on clean water and controlling Lake Okeechobee discharges, citing his experience as Juno Beach mayor.
Says he will focus on housing costs, property insurance, and cost-of-living stability, and opposes what he calls wasteful spending on projects such as the incumbent's support for renaming an airport.

candidates.researchNotes: His April 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey covers water, housing costs, insurance and spending; it does not address the guide's other issue topics, so no positions or statements were added. No campaign website was found.

candidates.name: David Fabrikant

priorities.text: Says he has drafted seven proposed laws, including taxing ammunition and restricting certain weapons for civilian use, tying the minimum wage to congressional salaries, and requiring corporations to disclose what share of their workforce is AI.
Says his policy priorities include economic support for lower-income people, public health, children's access to food, access to healthcare, and vaccination.

positions.summary: Lists a proposed law taxing ammunition and designating certain weapons as military, not for civilians.
positions.quote: A tax on ammunition/designation of certain weapons as military (not for civilians).

statements.quote: Tying minimum wage to congressional salaries, so the poor do not get left behind
statements.context: Among seven proposed laws in his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (May 2026)

statements.quote: The Trump Administration has attempted to isolate the United States. This has been done economically through the tariffs
Access to Healthcare - when people are forced to go without healthcare, to afford other necessities it results in a worsening of the health of the nation.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his May 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website was found.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for incumbent Brian Mast are added separately by script. James Martin has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions drawn from his campaign website. Alexander Cooke and David Fabrikant both completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; no FEC finance data is yet available for Fabrikant. Biographies rely on Ballotpedia, Mast's official site, and Martin's campaign 'Meet James' page; no campaign websites were found for Cooke or Fabrikant, and no Mast campaign site was reviewed.
